spans.text: "notes": "THE TWO-SIDED COINCIDENCE PIN (BACKFILL_DESIGN §6 as amended per PORTFOLIO_REVIEW F1), computed 2026-08-04 against the live baseline configuration (annotations_ext_v1_merged cbf50758.. + behavior_atoms_audit_v1 54056241.. + thresholds_frozen 60d1273a.., overlay-off legacy scorer vs dechained scoring, frozen cuts, snapshot rounding semantics). CLAUSE-SIDE CHAIN INVENTORY: 50 distinct chained names, 109 (name,clause) instances over 100 clauses. QUERY-SIDE: 7 chained query atoms — caution: must_preserve_user_agency__model_user, should_seek_confirmation__model_user; harm: shouldnot_lie_by_commission__model_third_party; helpfulness: should_ask_clarifying_questions__model_user, should_ask_followup_questions__model_user, should_disclose_lack_expertise__model_user, should_disclose_side_effects__model_user. DIRECTION (a) chained-query x chain-free-clause: only should_ask_clarifying_questions__model_user reaches new instances — the 13 chain-free clause instances m0027 m0100 m0106 m0107 m0108 m0156 m0183 m0188 m0374 m0380 m0387 m0457 m0474 (the F1 direction, confirmed verbatim); the other 6 chained query atoms reach 0 new instances (post chain-repair their clause-side instances carry the identical chain; no chain-free siblings exist). CRITICAL REFINEMENT OF F1: helpfulness's query ALSO carries the chain-free sibling should_ask_clarifying_questions, which already exact-matches those 13 clauses today — so under the join the two query entries collapse to one dechained key and the 13 clauses are REPRICED DOWN by the df-merge (df 13+2 -> 15, idf 3.7695 -> 3.6392; atom-channel delta -0.013721 raw on each), not newly matched; none of the 13 flips. m0384/m0385 (the chained clause instances, previously matched by the chained query atom at idf 5.2916) reprice to the merged idf 3.6392: atom-channel delta -0.174077 raw each. DIRECTION (b) chained-clause x chain-free-query: EMPTY — no chained clause name dechains onto any chain-free query atom of any DEV behaviour. DIRECTION (c) df-merge/global repricing: real merges should_ask_clarifying_questions df 15 (13+2), may_delegate_instruction_authority df 3+1 -> 4 (idf 5.0056 -> 4.7842), shouldnot_judge df {4 chained_mu, 1 chained_mud} -> 5 (idf -> 4.6035); the other 47 chained names are PURE RENAMES (df value preserved under the dechained key; vocabulary 628 -> 624 names); _atom_norm unchanged (5.695414224985685); lex channel: chain principal tokens leave 100 clauses' documents and 3 behaviours' query texts, shifting corpus term-idf globally by tiny amounts. NORMALIZER: helpfulness's raw corpus-max moves m0384 1.889654 -> m0438 1.807058 (the argmax clause itself repriced), so EVERY helpfulness normalized score rescales up ~4.5%; caution/harm normalized scores also move at the 3rd-4th decimal (592/593 clauses each) with zero predicted-set movement. FLIPS AT THE FROZEN CUTS: exactly 1 — helpfulness m0207 newly_predicted, 0.3048137341 -> 0.3169816964 vs frozen cut 0.3131186309, cause match_change under snapshot's taxonomy but NORMALIZER-DRIVEN: its raw score FELL (lex -0.0024, atom 0.0 exactly, section -0.0008); it crosses only because the corpus-max fell more. caution 95 -> 95, harm 73 -> 73, helpfulness 145 -> 146. max_regressions is set to 1, NOT 0, deliberately: we do not claim m0207 (an example block under 'Never generate sexual content involving minors') is panel-style relevant to helpfulness; we claim the flip's mechanism (atom delta exactly 0.0; pure normalizer rescale under a frozen cut). A 'regression' verdict there is a finding about reporting corpus-max-normalized scores under frozen cuts — the m0422 threshold-class question, CYCLE5_DESIGN I2's normalizer_drift class — not about dechained match semantics; either verdict is consistent with keeping the join, and the keep decision will cite the adjudication either way. ANY flip outside {m0207}, any no_longer_predicted flip, or any flip count != 1 falsifies this prediction. Chain-free parity: b8 bit-identical under the dechained path (computed True). GATE at MEASURE: snapshot.assert_frozen_thresholds on both snapshots (baseline verified PASS 2026-08-04)."
